questions: I'm new, where do I begin?
answers.answer:
Duracash makes sure finished work gets billed with everything the client needs, then follows the money until it's paid.
- Jobs, New job: job name, address, contract amount and the client, saved or new, with who signs off, its email and its phone. Retainage %, Contract number and Notes are on the same form.
- Add the day's diary, delivery tickets, photos, time sheets and invoices with New job record, or bring emails and texts in through the Inbox.
- Progress Pay App: enter this draw, the total done so far or a percent, then Draft Progress Pay App. Duracash holds back retainage and lists the supporting documents the client needs.
- Add each missing document, then Review & Send. It can go once nothing is missing.
- Record a payment when it arrives, send the waiver, ask for retainage at the end, then Finish job.
The Dashboard shows what needs you next.

questions: How do I create a job?
How do I add a new job?
Where do I enter a contract?
answers.answer: Go to Jobs and tap New job. Fill in Job name, the address (Street address, then City, State and ZIP) and Contract amount ($). Start date is today unless you change it; Anticipated end date is optional. Then tap Existing client and pick one, or New client and fill in Client name, Client type, Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps and Phone. A job needs all of these on its client. A saved client missing any of these shows those boxes right there, and what you type is saved to its Client playbook. If Who signs off on your bills only reads as the client's own name from an older save, the box is empty and you enter it once. Tap Save job. Have the contract as a Word file, a PDF or text? Tap Import contract first: it fills the boxes it finds, each marked From the contract, the contract's completion date goes in Anticipated end date, and the contract goes in the job records when you save. Below them: Retainage % (if the contract holds money back), Contract number and Notes (kept in the job records). A client you have saved before keeps its details; change them in Jobs, Client playbook.
follow_ups: What is the client type?
How do I bill progress on a job?

questions: How do I add a client?
Where do I add a client?
answers.answer: Go to Jobs, Client playbook and tap Add client. Fill in Client name, Client type, Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps and Phone: all of these are needed. Pay apps due by (day of the month), Payment terms, days and the Supporting documents needed with each pay app are yours to set or leave at the usual. Tap Add client. Have the contract? Tap Import a contract first: it fills the boxes it finds. A client can also be added with a job: tap New client on New job.

questions: How do I edit a job?
I made a typo in the job name
How do I delete a job?
Can I change the contract amount?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Edit job, next to its name. You can change the job name, the address (Street address, City, State and ZIP; a job saved with a one-line address shows it all in Street until you split it), contract number, Start date, Anticipated end date (never before the start date; blank clears it) and Retainage % (a new retainage applies from the next pay app). The contract amount can change only before the first pay app and without a schedule of values; a new job still on its one lump-sum line can change it until the first pay app is sent, and the line follows. After that, use a change order. The job code stays the same. Tap Save changes. Who signs off and the email for pay apps are in Jobs, Client playbook. In the Edit job form an owner also sees Delete job. It shows while the job has no payments and no pay app other than a deleted draft, so tap Delete Draft first if one is open. If a pay app was sent or a payment came in, finish the job instead.

questions: What does Who pays you? mean?
What does the role field mean?
What is the role on a new job?
answers.answer: Client type says what kind of client this is: General contractor, Owner or developer, Homeowner, Another subcontractor (you are a lower tier) or Public agency. It sets the supporting documents a new client starts with and when to follow up: a general contractor, or a subcontractor you work under, usually needs a lien waiver, an insurance certificate and daily tickets with every pay app; an owner, homeowner or public agency starts with an owner's list. It belongs to the client, so New job asks it only for a new client. Change it in Jobs, Client playbook.

questions: Can I use this on my phone?
answers.answer: There's no app-store app. Duracash runs in your phone's browser: sign in at the same address, and add it to your home screen from the browser's menu or Share button. On a phone, Take a photo opens the camera, in the Inbox, on a job and on a pay app's supporting documents, so you can photograph tickets straight onto a job.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: Can I add my office manager?
How do I invite my bookkeeper?
Can more than one person log in?
answers.answer: Yes. Someone who manages the team opens Settings, Team, enters Their email, picks a Profile and taps Invite. Invite stays off until your own email is confirmed; the Team page says so, with Send the link again. A profile says what a person can do. Owner can do everything. Member drafts pay apps, records payments and adds supporting documents; on Settings, Team, Permission profiles, an owner taps Edit on Member to give it more, such as Send pay apps, or New profile to add your own, like Office manager, with the permissions ticked. Only owners add or change profiles. To change someone's profile, pick another next to their name and tap Change. Everyone can draft, add records and follow up; the server refuses anything a person's profile doesn't allow. Every action is in the Activity log with the person's name. If the invite can't be emailed, you get a link to pass on; it works once, for 7 days.

questions: How do I edit a permission profile?
answers.answer: Only an owner can add, change or delete permission profiles. An owner opens Settings, Team and, under Permission profiles, taps Edit on a profile to change what it can do, New profile to add one (like Office manager) with the permissions ticked, or Delete on one they added. Owner is built in and can do everything. Anyone else sees what each profile can do but can't change it; someone who manages the team can still pick which profile a person has, next to their name.
follow_ups: Can I add my office manager?

questions: What's the difference between a pay app and an invoice?
Can I get a PDF of the pay app?
answers.answer: A pay app (pay application) is the bill for work done this period. It lists what was completed, line by line if the job has a schedule of values, adds signed change orders, and holds back retainage. Many contracts also need supporting documents with it. Open any pay app and tap Open the PDF; the same PDF goes with the email when you send it.
follow_ups: What are supporting documents?
What is retainage?

questions: How do I bill progress on a job?
How do I make a progress pay app?
Bill for work done this month
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Progress Pay App. Each schedule of values line is filled in with the total recorded to date, so what job records added up to is already there; change a figure to bill a different quantity. A lump-sum line is a % done. A job from before schedules were required with no schedule asks for This draw $, Total done so far $ or % complete instead. Tap Draft Progress Pay App. Duracash holds back retainage and lists the supporting documents from the client's settings. On the draft you can still change the dollars on any line. The job stays in progress.
follow_ups: What are supporting documents?
What is a draft for their review?

questions: Where do I start a new pay app?
Can I make a pay app from Money?
Create a pay application from the pay apps list
answers.answer: Two places, one way of drafting. On a job, tap Progress Pay App while the work goes on, or Draft Pay App after Final Pay App. Or on Money, Pay apps tap New pay app: with more than one job that has something to bill, pick it under Which job? and tap Continue. It opens that job's Progress Pay App form, or drafts it the way Draft Pay App does for a job marked done. A job isn't listed when it already has a draft open, including one waiting for the client's approval (open that draft with Review & Send), when its contract is billed in full, or, once marked done, when it has no work left to bill.
follow_ups: How do I bill progress on a job?

questions: How do I mark a job done?
The job is finished, what now?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Final Pay App. Fill in Anything to note? (optional) and Period to, tap Draft Final Pay App. A box shows the amount; if something is still pending, it says this will not be the final pay app. Confirm, and that records the work as finished, sets every schedule line to 100%, and Duracash drafts the final pay app for everything not billed yet. A draft that is still only here becomes the final pay app, keeping its number and supporting documents; one with the client for their review needs their answer (or Delete Draft) first, and the message names it. Every job also gets its closeout documents: the client's closeout items, or punch list sign-off, completion certificate, final lien waivers, as-builts and warranties. Tapped it by mistake? Undo Done works until the final pay app goes out.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?

questions: How do I send a pay app?
What does Fix things before sending mean?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Review & Send. The pay app page shows what the client will get: who it goes to, Also email (CC), the amount, the subject, the PDF to open, every file the email carries with a link to open it and Leave out or Put back, Add from the job records for an extra photo or receipt, the email's text, and any overrides and warnings. If your company address, phone or licence number is blank, it says so there with a Company details button; you can still send. Anything still missing is listed in Review & send, above the button, with Take a photo and Choose file. Then tap Approve & send to: it asks first, naming who it goes to, the amount and the period. While something is missing or an unsigned change order is on the pay app, the button says why under it instead of sending, and the job shows Fix N things before sending (or Add N missing documents, or Get CO N signed). The amounts, lines and approval are under Show the numbers. A General contractor, Public agency or Another subcontractor job at 0% retainage is named there too. If the email didn't go out, the page says so under the Sent pill. It goes to the client's Email for pay apps with the PDF and supporting documents attached, from your company name, and replies come back to you. A signed unconditional waiver attached to a pay app gives up your lien rights before you are paid, so sending is refused until you take it off or an owner types why and taps Send anyway. A file that only says one comes later, or a daily log that mentions one in passing, is shown with the words found: anyone who can send opens it and taps It's right. Who can send is set by each person's profile on Settings, Team. Communications, Outbox shows whether it was delivered.
follow_ups: What are supporting documents?
Did the client get my pay app?

questions: What is a draft for their review?
How do I send a pencil draft?
Can the GC review before I submit?
answers.answer: A draft for their review (pencil copy) is the draft pay app sent to the client to agree quantities and change orders before the real one, so nothing gets pushed to next month. It's optional. With a draft open, tap Send Draft for Their Review on the job. It opens the pay app with who it goes to, the amount, the PDF and the email, and any documents still missing, which don't hold it back. Tap Send Draft for Their Review there to email it. When they answer, tap Client Agreed to the Draft, or Client Wants Changes and note what they said.
follow_ups: How do I send a pay app?

questions: How do I delete a draft pay app?
answers.answer: Open the job, tap Delete Draft and confirm; only an owner can. The draft stays in the pay app list as Cancelled, any change order on it comes off, and you can draft again from the job page. The newest pay app on an open job can be withdrawn instead, if it was sent and nothing is paid on it (delete any newer draft first): an owner taps Pull back this pay app… on the pay app page, and the client is emailed that nothing is due on it.

questions: Why can't I draft a pay app?
answers.answer: Nothing to draft means all finished work is already on a pay app. Enter more progress with Progress Pay App, or tap Final Pay App first. If a draft is already open, Duracash says so and names it.

questions: What is a schedule of values?
Line items on a pay app
Can I bill by quantity and unit rate?
How do I set up a schedule of values?
Bill by quantities and unit rates
Import my schedule of values from Excel
answers.answer: A schedule of values breaks the contract into lines: a quantity at a unit rate (or a lump sum), with overhead and profit on top. Every new job has one: enter the lines on New job, or leave them blank and the job gets one lump-sum line for the contract amount. To change it, open the job and tap Enter schedule lines or Edit schedule on the Schedule of values card. Paste rows straight from Excel, Google Sheets, a CSV or your estimate PDF and tap Read pasted rows, or type them; then tap Save schedule. A row with a count but no price, like 3 loads, comes in with the unit rate blank and says it needs a price: enter it before you save. The total has to equal the contract. A schedule can be changed until the first pay app is sent, and a draft is updated from it. While a draft is with the client for their review the lines and rates are fixed, but quantities keep coming in. An older job with no schedule can add one until its first pay app is sent; after that it keeps billing in dollars, and the card says so. Quantities from job records add up on the card, under This billing period, to a suggested pay app value. Signed change orders add their own lines.

questions: How do I change the supporting documents for one job?
This job needs different supporting documents
answers.answer: Open the job and find Supporting documents for this job. It starts as the client's list. Tap Change for this job, tick or untick items, add others under Other, and tap Save supporting documents; Use the client's list goes back to it. The change applies from the next pay app and to a draft that hasn't been sent; a sent pay app stays as it went. The client's own list doesn't change, and the conditional waiver is still asked for. Certified payroll and Notarized pay application are on the list for public jobs: each is suggested from a job record of that kind with a file on it, and you check it, so file them as Certified payroll or Notarized pay application.
follow_ups: What are supporting documents?

questions: Why can't I start a pay app?
Why was my new job refused?
Client playbook is missing a phone
What does a client need before a job?
answers.answer: A new job needs a complete Client playbook: Client name, Client type, Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps and Phone. New job says which is missing under its box. A pay app on a job made under this rule waits the same way: the job page says what is missing, with Open Client playbook to add it. A job made before this rule keeps going as it is; its client is asked for what is missing the next time it gets a new job. Anyone on the team can fill in what is missing; changing what is saved takes the client settings permission.
follow_ups: How do I add a client?

questions: How is the suggested pay app value worked out?
Can I change the suggested pay app amount?
Change the amount on a pay app line
answers.answer: The Schedule of values card on the job shows This billing period: everything recorded and not yet billed, including late records. For each line it shows the quantity done, how much came from job records, what it adds up to and the suggested amount, then overhead and profit, retainage and the suggested amount due. You decide what is billed. On the Progress pay app form, change a line's quantity. On a draft, type a different amount in dollars in the line's box on the job's card or the pay app's page and tap Save amounts; clear the box or tap Back to the suggested amounts to undo it. An amount can be anything from $0 to what is left on the line. Your amount stays when more job records come in, with the new suggestion beside it, and the Activity log keeps the suggested and final amounts. A line billed short is suggested again on the next pay app. A final pay app bills all that is left. On the Progress pay app form, a blank box bills the suggested amount, and a draft you delete or pull back takes its typed figures with it. A wrong quantity in the field: tap Correct field total on the line, or Undo import on the file's entry in Job records. Both are kept in the Activity log with the old and new totals, and sent pay apps stay as they are.

questions: Why does a pay app need a packet?
answers.answer: Supporting documents are everything the contract says must go with a pay app: lien waivers, delivery tickets, photos, signed change orders, schedule of values, insurance certificate. Duracash lists the items from the job's list (Supporting documents for this job on the job page), which starts as the client's (Supporting documents needed with each pay app), and won't send the pay app until each one is in. Every pay app also asks for a conditional lien waiver unless the client was marked as not taking one. It is part of the pay app: see it under Supporting documents on the pay app's page, from the Supporting documents column of Money, Pay apps or Supporting documents on the job.
follow_ups: How do I add missing supporting documents?
How do I change what a client needs?

questions: How do I add missing supporting documents?
How do I add missing paperwork?
How do I clear a packet item?
How do I mark something present?
How do I attach a document to the packet?
What does I have this mean?
answers.answer:
On the job, tap Add N missing documents (or Fix N things before sending, or Open Supporting Documents): it opens the pay app, with what is missing in Review & send. An item clears when a real file is on it and a person has checked it; the title doesn't matter. For each missing item:
- Take a photo or Choose file: it goes in the job records, and adding it records that you checked it. A photo or scan the check can't read says Photo added by you, and is in.
- Under From the job records this period, pick Attach to… on a record, then Attach.
- A file Duracash found in the job records: open it and tap I checked this file.
- If a warning names what didn't match (the job name, the amount, the conditional wording), or says a file looks blank, open the document and tap I opened it and it's right (one tap), or Remove it.
- I have this…: an override. Enter the reason, for example "emailed to the GC on 10/12", then Save override. The pay app and Review & send show who overrode it, when and why; the client sees only the tick.
- Not needed for this client, if they never need it.
Remove takes an item back off while the pay app is a draft. The Activity log shows how each item was handled.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: How do I change what a client needs?
How do I change what a customer needs?
How do I change what a payer requires?
Who signs off on my bills?
What is the email for pay apps?
Where do I see my clients?
answers.answer: Jobs, Client playbook keeps each client's rules. Open a client to change Who signs off on your bills, Email for pay apps, Days between follow-ups, Days they usually take to pay, Client type, Supporting documents needed with each pay app (tick each item, add the rest under Other, or tick Nothing needed), They send pay apps back when, Also email (CC) and more, then tap Save client. New pay apps use the supporting documents list, unless a job has changed its own. Once saved, Who signs off, Email for pay apps and Phone can be changed but not removed. When a client sends a pay app back, add the reason to They send pay apps back when and tap Save client. While something is blocking send on a job, you can also note it there under Client Sent Pay App Back. Each client also lists its open and finished jobs, with a link to each job's contract and Add contract. Add client takes the same details, and Import a contract fills them from the contract. Changing a saved client takes Edit company details, client settings and connections on the Team page. Without it the card is read only, and it asks only for what the client is still missing, the same as New job.

questions: I have the same client twice
I have the same customer twice
How do I delete a customer?
How do I merge two customers?
How do I rename a customer?
Why does it ask Same as another customer?
answers.answer: All three are in Jobs, Client playbook. To rename a client, open it, change Client name and tap Save client. Saved the same client twice? Open the one to drop, use Same client as another one?, pick the one to keep and tap Merge. Its jobs move over. An owner can tap Delete client on a client no job uses, finished jobs included. One with jobs can't be deleted, but you can merge it into another client. Renaming, merging and deleting take Edit company details, client settings and connections on the Team page. When you add a job or a client with a name close to a saved one, like ABC Builders Inc for ABC Builders, Duracash asks Same as ABC Builders? Tap Use ABC Builders, or keep the new name to add a second client.
follow_ups: How do I change what a client needs?

questions: How do I add a change order?
Extra work the customer asked for
answers.answer: Open the job and tap New Change Order, or tap New Change Order on Money, Change orders and pick the job. Enter a Title, pick the Reason (owner request, unforeseen condition, design issue, value engineering or other; Other needs a description) and the Amount ($), negative for a credit. You can also add cost lines (their total becomes the amount), pick lump sum or time and materials, name the contract section it changes, tick backup from the job records and enter the day work started. Tap Create change order. It stays Unsigned until the client signs: tap Request signature to email them a signing link, or Signed on paper…, enter who signed it and the date, and Save as signed with the signed copy (Take a photo of the signed copy adds it to the job records). Once signed it adds to the contract and is billable on the next pay app, even after the job is done. If work started before it was signed, it shows Work started before signing.
follow_ups: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
The client won't sign the change order

questions: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
Put a change order on the pay app before it's signed
Can I bill a change order that isn't signed yet?
Change order not signed, can I bill it?
answers.answer: Yes. On the job's Change orders card, tap Bill now (send waits for signature) on the unsigned change order. Its dollars go on the open draft (drafted again with it, same number) or on the next pay app, but that pay app can't be sent until the change order is signed: the job shows Get CO N signed. An unsigned change order never goes out by accident.

questions: The client won't sign the change order
The customer won't sign the change order
answers.answer: Tap Withdraw on the unsigned change order and confirm. If it is on an open draft, an owner deletes that draft first (Delete Draft), then withdraw the change order and draft again. A withdrawn change order stays in history.

questions: How do I record a payment?
The customer paid, what do I do?
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Record a payment. Pick the Pay app, check Amount received ($) (it starts at what is owed), Date received and Check or reference no. (optional), then tap Record. Less than owed leaves the pay app Partly paid; paid in full opens the waiver step for that pay app. The amount can't be more than what is owed, and a reference can only be used once per job. Many payments at once? Read a QuickBooks export on Import/Export, Import.
follow_ups: What is a lien waiver?
Does it connect to QuickBooks?

questions: They only paid part of it
They paid only part of the pay app
Customer paid less than the bill
answers.answer: Record what came in with Record a payment. The pay app shows Partly paid with the rest still owed, and no waiver is due until it's paid in full. Follow up on the balance from Money, Unpaid. If the rest won't come, an owner taps Accept $X short pay…, gives the reason and confirms.

questions: Why do I need a waiver?
answers.answer: A lien waiver gives up your lien rights for money you've been paid. Conditional: it only takes effect if the payment clears; one goes with each pay app. Unconditional: payment received; you send it once the pay app is paid. Some states require exact statutory forms, so use the form your state or the client requires; Duracash doesn't write it. The waiver page names the form for the job's state where it knows it (Georgia so far).
follow_ups: How do I send a waiver?

questions: How do I send a waiver?
answers.answer: When a pay app is paid in full, the job shows Choose waiver and send (the Dashboard shows Waiver due). Put the signed waiver of that type in the job records first (New job record, Other documents and notes, kind: Lien waiver), or tap Take a photo on the waiver page; Approve & send stays off until it is there. Pick the type; the line under it says when it fits, and Check the signed form shows lists what the form must carry. Then tap Approve & send and confirm. The email attaches that signed waiver, never one that already went out with a pay app. One waiver per paid pay app and per retainage release, and only after the payment is recorded. Take the photo from that pay app's row so the waiver is tied to it; when a signed waiver isn't tied and more than one is due, the page asks which pay app it is for before it can go. Handed the waiver over yourself, or the client doesn't need one? Open Not needed, or handed over outside Duracash…, say why and tap Mark not needed: it is kept on the pay app and in the activity log, and the job can be finished. A client marked Not needed for this client on the conditional waiver owes no waiver after payment either. Duracash doesn't write waiver forms; states set them. Duracash reads the file as it goes: if it is blank, a scan, or says another type, job or amount, it names what didn't match, and the waiver goes only once you say you opened it and it's right. A final waiver is suggested only when nothing is left to bill or collect on the job.
follow_ups: Which waivers are due?

answers.answer: Retainage is a percentage (often 5 to 10) the client holds back from every pay app until the job is closed out. Duracash holds it back on each pay app, shows it as a line, and tracks it as Held back, still owed until it's paid.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?
Which jobs are holding my retainage?

questions: How do I get retainage released?
How do I ask for retainage?
How do I get my retainage back?
How do I get retainage paid?
When do I get my retainage?
answers.answer: Retainage is paid at closeout, so it is asked for after Final Pay App. The closeout documents is the client's closeout items, or punch list sign-off, completion certificate, final lien waivers, as-builts and warranties; mark one Not needed on this job if it doesn't apply. Tap Final Pay App, add those items (Open Closeout Documents), then tap Ask for Retainage and confirm, or type part of it in the amount box on Money, Closeout. The job's Retainage card shows what is held, the pay apps holding it, how often you asked and when you can ask again. When the money arrives, tap Record Retainage Paid on the job; each release then needs its lien waiver.
follow_ups: Which jobs are holding my retainage?

questions: How do I log a conversation?
I called them about the payment
Note a phone call with the client
answers.answer: Open the job and tap Log a Conversation, or tap it on New job record, or on a Follow up row on the Dashboard. Enter what they said and tap Save. It goes on the job's records under Conversations. While a pay app is waiting for payment it counts as a follow-up, so the next one waits the client's usual days. Enter Check again on and the next follow-up waits until that date instead.
follow_ups: How do follow-up windows work?

answers.answer: Each client has Days between follow-ups in Jobs, Client playbook (7 if blank). Once that many days have passed since the pay app was sent (or since the last follow-up), the Dashboard shows a Follow up row and the job shows Send Follow-Up. Before then, Money, Unpaid shows the next follow-up date, and Follow Up Now on the job sends one early. Each follow-up is emailed to the client's Email for pay apps and listed in the Outbox; from the third one it also copies Also email from the third follow-up.

Automations is where you choose your own reminders: important dates, missing information, and change order work on a job record that lacks what it needs. Tick In the app, Email or Text for each, then Save. All are off until you turn them on. Each comes round every 3 days until it is dealt with, and email and text go out at most once a day. Notifications in the app are listed there with an unread count. Reminders go to you and your team, never to clients. The Dashboard's To Do still shows each follow-up when it is due.
follow_ups: How do follow-up windows work?

questions: How do I get text reminders?
answers.answer: No, Duracash never texts clients. Clients hear from you by email. Texts are only for your own team: add your mobile number and agree to texts on Settings, My account, enter the code we text to that number, then tick Text for a reminder on Automations. Reply STOP to any text to turn them off.

questions: Where do I see unpaid pay apps?
answers.answer: Money, Unpaid lists every job with money owed: what is unpaid, days since it was sent, when it's due, when they said they'd pay, who to contact, and buttons to send a follow-up, email or call. Open Recent contact under a job to see the last emails, calls and client page visits, newest first, and See all on the job for its whole history.
follow_ups: Who owes me money?

questions: Did the client get my pay app?
Did the customer get my pay app?
Where do I see what I sent?
Who does the email come from?
answers.answer: Communications, Outbox lists every email you approved and what happened to it: sent (with the time), failed (with the reason, such as an address the client's mail server refused), or not sent. A failed or unsent email has a Send Again button once the server sends mail, the Dashboard shows a Didn't go out row, and a pay app's page says so under its Sent pill. Pay apps go out with the PDF and supporting documents attached, from "your company via Duracash", and the client's reply goes to whoever sent it. Each email lists what it carried (open any file from there) and has Print. The demo account never sends real email.

Each email in Communications, Outbox has Print: it prints that one email with who it went to, when, its status, the message and what it carried. Each row of Everything received on Communications, Inbox has Print too, for something that came in. For a pay app, open it and tap Open the PDF, then print the PDF.
follow_ups: Where do I see what I sent?
Where is everything received?

answers.answer: No. Automated calls to clients need prior consent under federal law and are not planned before a lawyer reviews it. Money, Unpaid has a Call button that opens your phone, when the client has a phone number.

questions: How do I import emails and texts?
How do I upload a document?
Can I bring in my supporting documents?
Can I bring in my paperwork?
How do I upload a file?
How do I upload a pdf or photo?
answers.answer:
Three ways:
- Drop files anywhere, or tap Take a photo or Add a file on a job (photos, PDFs, Word, Excel, CSV, saved emails). On a job page they go straight onto that job; Jobs, New job record has a place for each kind of document on the job you pick; elsewhere they wait in the Inbox. Import/Export, Import has Which job?, Take a photo and Choose files.
- Paste an email, a text thread or your notes on Import/Export, Import and tap Add to Inbox.
- Forward email and texts automatically once an owner connects an email service and a Twilio number (Inbox, Bring emails and texts in automatically).
The Inbox suggests the job from the job code, address, job name or sender; tap Add to (the job) to file it.
follow_ups: How do I import 30 days of notes?
How does it know which job?

questions: How do I import 30 days of notes?
answers.answer: Copy the notes, paste them on Import/Export, Import with "Notes: one job record per date" picked, and tap Add to Inbox. Start each day with a date (10/12, Oct 12, or 2026-10-12). Duracash splits them into one job record per date and keeps the original date when you add them to a job.

questions: How does it know which job?
Why didn't it suggest a job?
answers.answer: It looks for the job code (like VEST), the job address, the job name or a part of it no other job has (like Oak Street for Oak Street kitchen), the client's name, or an email from the client's email for pay apps. A code in small letters (vest) or one word of a job name (Vesta) counts less than who sent it, so everyday words don't pull an item to another client's job. If a few jobs fit equally, it lists them to pick from and doesn't guess. Tip: put the job code in capitals in email subjects and texts. Tap Other job to change it before adding, and Undo under Everything received (Communications, Inbox) takes an added item back off; each row there says how it came in and why it was matched. If a pay app's supporting documents use it, Undo says so and links there: tap Remove on a draft's supporting documents first; one that went to the client stays as sent.

questions: How do I forward emails to Duracash?
answers.answer: Automatic email needs an email service that posts incoming mail to a web address (SendGrid, Mailgun or Postmark); automatic texts need a Twilio number. An owner opens Bring emails and texts in automatically in the Inbox for the private addresses to paste into those services. Until they're connected, save emails as .eml or paste them, and paste or screenshot texts. Once texts are connected, a text with photos or PDFs waits in the Inbox, saying who sent it when the number is on a team member's My account, until an owner, or someone allowed to edit company details, files it to a job. A number nobody on the team has shows as Unknown sender.

questions: What file types can I upload?
answers.answer: PDF, JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, HEIC, Word (.doc, .docx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), CSV, TXT and saved emails (.eml), up to 15 MB each. Drop the file on any page (on a job page it goes straight onto that job), or use Choose files on Import/Export, Import (Take a photo or Choose files on a phone). Web pages and SVG files are refused for safety.

questions: What is a new job record?
How do I log what happened today?
How do I add a delivery ticket, time sheet or invoice?
answers.answer: New job record is one form for what happened on site and the day's documents. Go to Jobs, New job record (or tap New job record on a job), pick the Job and the Date, then fill in what you have and tap Save job record. The Diary, Crew members, Weather and Materials cover the day. Tick Quantities, Change order work or New punchlist items to add those. Delivery tickets, Progress photos, Time sheets, Invoices and Inspections each have their own section with Take a photo and Choose files, and Other documents and notes takes every other kind, such as an insurance certificate or a warranty. Each file or filled section becomes its own record of that kind in the job's Job records, ready to go with the supporting documents a pay app needs. A document alone needs no Diary. If an upload fails, what you typed and the files not sent yet stay, so you can save again. Quantities put in place today add to each schedule of values line's total and move the suggested pay app value on the job's Schedule of values card; a lump-sum line takes the % done today. They don't change a draft: Progress Pay App brings them in. The part of a quantity past what is scheduled, or a lump sum past 100%, isn't added, and neither are quantities on a finished job. The record is still saved with them on it, and it says why under Quantities. Or paste many days of notes at once on Import/Export, Import; they wait in the Inbox to be added to the job.

questions: How do I import quantities from my own records?
Bring in quantities from my estimating or accounting software
answers.answer: On Import/Export, Import, under Quantities done, pick the Job (only jobs with a schedule of values are listed), then tap Choose the file for a CSV or Excel file, or paste the rows and tap Read quantities. Each row needs the item number or description of a schedule line and the quantity done this period; a lump sum line takes the % done this period. The table shows each row: the line, Done to date, Add, New total and Scheduled, and why a row can't be added (no line matches, the item number and description name different lines, the quantity is in another unit or is a % on a line that isn't a lump sum, it would go past the scheduled quantity or, with stored materials, past the line's value, the line is twice in the file). Nothing changes until you tap Add to the schedule of values: then the rows that can go on add to each line's total and move the suggested pay app value, the same as a job record's quantities. Progress pay app bills them. What couldn't be added is listed, and the import is kept in the job records.
follow_ups: What is a daily record?

answers.answer: Dashboard, Calendar starts with Tasks: your To Do items and the calendar's dates for This week, Next week, This month or a Custom range, each opening its day, with Add task. Below it the month shows anticipated end dates, work complete, pay apps sent, follow-ups due, expected approvals, payments, waivers and pay app due dates for the open jobs. Pick a job in the Job filter to see only that job. A finished job leaves the calendar; its dates stay in its job file. Tap a day for its events. These are your billing dates, not legal deadlines.
follow_ups: Can I put this on Google Calendar?

questions: Can I put this on Google Calendar?
answers.answer: Yes. In Dashboard, Calendar, open "Put these dates on your phone". On an iPhone or a Mac, tap Add to my phone's calendar. Or copy the private address, and in Google Calendar on a computer choose Other calendars, +, From URL. Outlook can subscribe to the same address. Calendar apps refresh it on their own schedule, often every few hours.

questions: When do I have to file a lien?
answers.answer: Not yet. Lien and notice deadlines depend on the state, your role and the project type, and a wrong date can cost lien rights, so Duracash won't calculate them until they're reviewed by a lawyer for a specific state. The calendar shows billing dates only.

questions: How do I export my data?
Can I get my data out?
Export payments and change orders as CSV
answers.answer: Everything you can export is on Import/Export, Export. Lists for a spreadsheet (CSV) has Jobs, Pay apps, Payments and Change orders, finished jobs included, for anyone on the team. Anyone whose profile includes Export and reset data (owners do) taps Download everything for your company's jobs, clients, pay apps and records as one file; anyone can download each sent pay app's PDF and QuickBooks file, and copy the calendar feed. Photos and documents you uploaded are not in it, so keep your own copies of those.

Open Settings, Company, Your data, and tap Reset data (it needs a profile with Export and reset data; owners have it). Reset deletes every job, client and record in your company; a snapshot is kept on the server first. To confirm, type the company name exactly and your password, then tap Reset everything. On the demo account, Reset the demo puts the sample data back.

On the sign-in screen, click Forgot your password? and enter your email: a reset link arrives that works once, for one hour, and signs you out everywhere else. Signed in, open Settings, My account and tap Change password: on its own page, tap Email me a code, then type the code, your current password and the new one (where the server can't send email yet, the current password is enough). Every other device is signed out. After 3 wrong passwords for one email, each new try has to wait a little longer, up to a minute. After 20 wrong passwords from one network, sign-in from that network pauses for 15 minutes. Passwords need at least 10 characters. If the server can't send email yet, the screen says so; ask the Duracash team.

Each company's data is kept separate; only your team's logins can open it, apart from the private links you share: the Calendar address and each client's page. Those who manage the team decide who is on it and what each person can do. Signing in from a new device asks for a second step (a code by email, or from an authenticator app), and you are signed out after an hour without use. Passwords are stored as one-way hashes; reset links work once and expire. Duracash is still early: keep your own copies of signed documents, and use Download everything (Import/Export, Export) for a copy. Questions you ask here are saved so the team can add better answers.
This helper answers from a library of prepared answers and your own job data; it isn't an AI model. When AI features arrive, you'll approve everything they send.

Yes. On Import/Export, Import, under Payments from QuickBooks, paste or choose a QuickBooks payments export (CSV or Excel) and tap Read payments: each payment is matched to its pay app where Duracash can tell (pick one from the Pick a pay app… list for the rest), and Record the ticked payments records the ones you tick. Or an owner taps Connect QuickBooks (when it is set up on the server): Then tap Read payments from QuickBooks, tick the ones to keep and tap Record the ticked payments. Duracash never changes your books. Each sent pay app also has Download for QuickBooks, a file QuickBooks imports as an invoice.
There are no direct connections to other software yet. Duracash sits beside the tools you use: export reports, photos or PDFs from them and drop the files into the Inbox.

The free trial is timed to the payment cycle: nothing to pay until the first pay app you send through Duracash is paid, or 90 days, whichever comes first (120 if a pay app is still unpaid on day 90). After the trial it is $299 a month, with no cut of what you collect. A company that bills homeowners in draws gets 45 days or the first paid draw. Settings, Billing shows where your trial stands. An owner taps Subscribe in Settings, Billing and pays by card through Stripe.

questions: I need help from a human
answers.answer: Email the Duracash founders at the address under Contact at the end of the Privacy Policy (/privacy). Tell them what you clicked and what you expected; a screenshot helps. Questions you ask here are saved, so they also see what's missing.

questions: What does the Overview page show?
answers.answer: Dashboard, Overview starts with To Do: what to do next, most urgent first, each with its button, whose court it is in (Us or Client), who it is assigned to and when it is due. Pick Mine or Everyone, and This week, This month, Today or a Date range; overdue items always show. Below it are Done, not billed, Outstanding, Held back, still owed and Billed this month, how many jobs are active and how many can't be sent yet, then a table of jobs you can filter (Ready to send, Can't send yet, Unpaid, Waiver due, Completed this month). Hover a label and tap its (i) for what it means.

questions: How do I assign a task to someone?
How do I add a task?
What does ball in court mean?
answers.answer: On Dashboard, Overview, the To Do list shows each item's Ball in court (Us when someone here has to act, Client when you are waiting on the client), its Assignee and its Due date. Pick a name in an item's Assignee box to assign it; anyone on the team can. Change the date in its Due box to set when it is due; clear it to go back to the item's own date. Tap Add task for something of your own: what needs doing, and optionally the job, who, when and whose court. Tap Done when it is finished. Each person's morning email lists what is assigned to them (a pay app due soon is listed as soon as it shows, so there's time to get it ready; an item you dated for a later day waits for that day), and an owner's also lists what nobody has. When someone leaves the team, their open items and the jobs assigned to them go to the owner who removed them.

Each job has a short status, such as Needs supporting documents, Blocked, Ready to send, Sent, Partly paid or Waiver due, and a line that names what's holding it up, for example "Conditional waiver on progress payment is missing" or "Submitted, awaiting acknowledgment". It never just says pending. The Next column says what to do.

Settings, Activity log lists every action: what happened, when, who (the signed-in person) and what kind of action. Pick a job in the Job filter to see only that job; finished jobs are listed after the open ones. Without the app's own entries leaves out what Duracash wrote itself (files suggested from the job records, document checks). A job's Activity shows one entry per action, with that bookkeeping folded under it.

questions: What are the little i icons?
answers.answer: Hover any label, column or tile: a small (i) appears next to it. Hover or tap the (i) to see what that field means. On a phone, each card has a "What do these mean?" list instead.

questions: How do I finish a job?
How do I close a job?
Why can't I close this job?
answers.answer: Finishing a job takes the Finish and reopen jobs permission, which owners have. Finish job appears when the work is done and nothing is left: no open draft, no unsigned change order, nothing unbilled or unpaid, retainage paid and waivers sent. Until then the job page shows Before you can finish this job, one line per thing with a button for each. Tap Finish job and confirm: the job moves to Jobs, Job history and leaves the working lists. Its page becomes its job file: what it came to, every pay app with its PDF, payments, change orders, waivers sent, the job records and its activity, with Download job file for all of it in one zip. Anyone with that permission can tap Add more work to open the same job again, for more work or a late payment.

questions: How do I delete my account?
answers.answer: Only the Company Admin can delete the company: the one owner shown on Settings, Team (at first, the person who created the company; they can hand the role to another owner with Hand over). The Company Admin opens Settings, Company, Your data, taps delete the company, types their password and the company name, then taps Delete everything. It removes every job, file, client and record, and every user on the team, at once. Use Download everything (Import/Export, Export) first if you want a copy. Server backups that already hold the data expire on their own (the newest 14 are kept by default).
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Do you back up my data?
What if the server loses my data?
answers.answer: Yes. The server makes a backup every 24 hours (and on start-up when the last one is older) and keeps the newest 14. Those copies sit on the server and guard against mistakes and bugs. When off-site backup is set up, each one is also encrypted and copied off the server. Keep your own copy too, with Download everything on Import/Export, and keep signed documents outside Duracash.
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Why do I need to confirm my email?
I didn't get the confirmation email
My emails say verify your email first
answers.answer: Duracash sends pay apps with replies coming back to the person who sent them, so it checks that the address is really yours first. Tap the link in the confirmation email (it works for 3 days). Didn't get it? Use Send the link again in Settings, My account, then check spam. Emails held while you were unconfirmed have Send Again in the Outbox.

questions: Where are the terms of service?
What do you do with my data?
answers.answer: The Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy are linked at the bottom of the sign-in page (/terms and /privacy). In short: your data is yours, we use it only to run Duracash for you, we don't sell it or use it for advertising, the app loads no tracking scripts, and an owner can export or delete everything. Both pages say if they are still a draft awaiting a lawyer's review.
follow_ups: Is my data safe?

questions: Why did I get a sign-in code?
answers.answer: Two-step sign-in is on for every account, so a stolen password isn't enough. Signing in from a new device asks for a 6-digit code we email to you; tick Don't ask again on this device for 30 days to skip it on that device. If the code can't be emailed, you aren't signed in; try again shortly. For a stronger second step, open Settings, My account and tap Use an authenticator app instead: scan the QR code, type the code and save the recovery codes. It can't be turned off. Where the server can't send email yet, the authenticator app is the second step, and setting it up is asked right after you sign in (Not now puts it off).

Yes. Open Settings, My account, Appearance: pick Theme (Same as this device, Light or Dark) and an Accent colour, then tap Save at the bottom. It is kept with your account, so it follows you to every device; your teammates keep their own. Pay app PDFs and your clients' pages stay as they are.

Duracash signs you out after an hour without use, so a screen left open isn't left signed in. Two minutes before, a note says Signing you out in 2 minutes with Stay signed in. Sign in again and the page you had open comes back.
